title: The Checklist
coreMove: Separate vital minimum checks from expert knowledge and make those checks visible at the moment they are skipped.
sourcePressure: The source anchors this chapter in the B-17 flight-test story, recurring expert failures of forgetting and skipping, and Pronovost's central-line checklist in the Keystone Initiative.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version treats a checklist as a comprehensive task list. The real move is to protect the few basic actions that are deadly when skipped.

sourceAnchors.name: B-17 flight-test story
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies the B-17 story as the case where one missed basic defeated elite aviation skill.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The B-17 story carries the hard lesson: a machine can be too advanced for courage and memory alone.

sourceAnchors.name: Pronovost
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar names Pronovost's central-line checklist and the Keystone Initiative as evidence that short lists can cut infections and save lives.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Pronovost's list did not teach doctors what a central line was; it made the life-saving basics harder to skip.

sourceAnchors.name: Keystone Initiative
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar links the Keystone Initiative to central-line checklist evidence in intensive care.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Keystone matters because the checklist made private confidence answer to a shared minimum.

hook: The checklist is humble but powerful
counterintuition: A checklist is not for amateurs
The basics are what experts forget
tryThisNow: Write your own checklist before your next task

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Claire, an anesthesia resident at the pre-induction pause
exampleSpecs.audience: medical trainees who know the steps but face rushed rooms
exampleSpecs.stakes: antibiotics and airway backup are assumed complete before incision
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire reads only the three non-negotiable checks aloud and catches the missing antibiotic before the drape goes up
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 7:06 a.m., Claire sees the empty antibiotic line beside the anesthesia cart

exampleSpecs.domain: Lukas, a community pool operator opening for swim lessons
exampleSpecs.audience: seasonal supervisors who rely on habit after years of routine
exampleSpecs.stakes: children enter the water before chemical levels are verified
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lukas stops the gate opening until the chlorine reading, rescue tube, and drain cover check are marked in front of the lifeguards
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the sharp smell of chlorine hanging over a silent pool deck

exampleSpecs.domain: Anya, a mobile blood drive coordinator
exampleSpecs.audience: nursing teams setting up temporary clinical spaces
exampleSpecs.stakes: a donor reaction becomes harder to handle if the emergency kit is still in the van
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anya asks the team to point to the emergency kit and donor ID scanner before the first donor sits down
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Show me the kit before we open," Anya says in the church basement

exampleSpecs.domain: David, a commercial bakery allergen-line supervisor
exampleSpecs.audience: food production leads who see repeated cleaning as obvious
exampleSpecs.stakes: an almond residue miss sends mislabeled pastries to a school order
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: David reduces the changeover list to swab, label roll, and bin seal, then makes the line lead verify them before restart
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took David one returned tray to stop trusting the changeover from memory

exampleSpecs.domain: Camille, a fire station lieutenant checking the truck
exampleSpecs.audience: first responders who prize speed but depend on ready equipment
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missing oxygen cylinder turns up only after the engine is rolling
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille asks the crew which three items would stop them cold on a call, then verifies those before letting the full inventory distract them
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which missing item would make the siren useless?

exampleSpecs.domain: Akira, a photo lab manager processing film
exampleSpecs.audience: craft workers who think skill protects routine sequence
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wedding roll is ruined if chemical temperature is assumed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira posts a two-check strip at the developer tank and makes temperature and fixer freshness visible before the roll is opened
exampleSpecs.firstImage: red safelight pooling over a stainless developer tank

skillTargets: evaluate whether verification is shared and visible

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one repeated task and cross out every item except the three omissions that could cause real harm, delay, or rework.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
